topic: The art of medicine: arts-based training in observation and mindfulness for fostering the empathic response in medical residents

sources.title: The art of medicine: arts-based training in observation and mindfulness for fostering the empathic response in medical residents
sources.authors: Zazulak J, Sanaee M, Frolic A, Knibb N, Tesluk E, Hughes E, Grierson LEM.

findings.finding: Arts-based training that includes dance and mindfulness can improve a learner's self-confidence and communication abilities.
findings.quote: The results indicated that programme participants improved in the Mindfulness Scale domains related to self-confidence and communication relative to a group of control participants following the arts-based programme.

findings.finding: Engaging with arts-based curricula helps foster empathy and supports the personal well-being of trainees.
findings.quote: The study concludes that a multifaceted arts-based curriculum focusing on evidence-based observation and mindfulness is a useful tool in bolstering the empathic response, improving communication, and fostering professional well-being among medical residents.

principle: Integrating arts-based observation and mindfulness practices can enhance communication skills and professional well-being in learners.
for_the_teacher: Incorporate mindfulness exercises before or after dance practice to help learners cultivate presence and self-awareness.
Encourage learners to practice 'visual literacy' by observing and describing the movement qualities of others to build empathy and observational skills.
when_it_does_not_apply: The study focused specifically on medical residents in obstetrics, gynaecology, and family medicine, and results on psychometric measures were mixed.
